paragraphs: On Thursday after lunch, Ranger Mark came to the school. The Explorers met him on the sports court, because it was cool under the roof. He wore his green cap and brown boots, and he had a big bag. Teacher Kim sat next to the children on a long bench. The court was quiet, and everybody looked at him. "Today I will tell you about my work," he said. Lily opened her notebook and wrote a title.

Ranger Mark began with his career. "I wanted to work in a forest when I was your age," he said. "I studied for four years, and then I got my first job in the nature park." "A ranger has many jobs." "I walk in the forest, I look after the animals, and I talk to visitors." "Is it a hard career?" asked May. "Sometimes it is hard, but I like it every day," he said. He smiled at May.

Next, he talked about the rainforest in the nature park. "A rainforest is warm and wet, and it has many kinds of animals." "The tall trees make a green roof, and only a little light comes down." "Insects, birds, monkeys, and frogs live there." "Some live high in the trees, and some live on the ground." Lily wrote two words: green roof. Mia asked, "Which animal is the hardest to see?" "Probably the small ones," said Ranger Mark with a smile.

After that, he told the children about an international bird count. "Every year, rangers from many countries count birds at the same time," he said. "Their forests are similar to ours, so they count in the same way." "The numbers are sent to one big list on a computer." "Then scientists can see if there are more birds or fewer birds each year." "So our birds help scientists in other countries?" asked Leo. "Yes, and that is a good fact to know," said Ranger Mark. Leo smiled, and he sat up straight.

At the end, Ranger Mark asked, "Can the Explorers count birds in the school garden?" "Yes, we can," said Teacher Kim. She looked very pleased. "We can count among the trees every Thursday." Lily wrote the plan on a new page of her notebook. Mia will take the photos, and May will write the numbers. Leo said, "I will make a poster, and I will put it on the court." Lily wrote the first line: "Birds in Our School Garden."
